newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq sees no need for dialogue with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Iraq sees no need for dialogue with U.S..

text.p: Iraq is not interested in dialogue with the United States and Washington's dreams of a change in Iraq's government will vanish into thin air, the ruling Baath party newspaper said in a front-page editorial on Wednesday.
"You Americans go to hell," Thawra said. "We are not in need of carrying out a dialogue with you and do not wish for it to happen."

The editorial was in reaction to what the newspaper said were anti-Iraq remarks Frederick Smith, U.S. Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defence for International Security Affairs, made in Bahrain on Tuesday.

"This Smith made a haughty and arrogant statement yesterday in which he said America will not talk to Iraq unless there is a change in the present regime," the newspaper said, quoting the U.S. official.

"But we say to this Smith and other American officials...We are staying here at the head of the Arabian Gulf ... a strong and robust country ... and may you and all of you go to hell once again," it said.
Iraq in the past showed readiness to enter a dialogue with Washington but Thawra said U.S. officials ..."would be stupid to think" ... that such calls were made from a position of weakness.

The United States, which led the multi-national force that ousted Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991, says it currently sees no alternative to maintaining sanctions against Iraq as long a President Saddam Hussein remains in power.
